title: Informational Thermodynamics: The Velocity of Collapse. Why Intelligent Systems Collapse at Different Speeds

detail.title: Informational Thermodynamics: The Velocity of Collapse. Why Intelligent Systems Collapse at Different Speeds
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Informational Thermodynamics, a physics-inspired framework explaining why AI and knowledge systems collapse at different rates across industries. Instead of treating failure as a timing or lifecycle problem, the study models semantic degradation as an entropy-driven velocity phenomenon governed by a domain-specific drift constant (λ).

Across finance, law, and medicine, systems traverse the same recursive decay sequence (C₀–C₄), but differ structurally in how fast semantic integrity deteriorates. Five parameters—semantic density, decision velocity, interpretive tolerance, error asymmetry, and redundancy—determine λ and therefore collapse velocity. The framework explains why high-velocity domains degrade rapidly despite fluent outputs, while redundancy-rich domains decay more slowly.

The paper positions Enterprise Semantic Integrity (ESI) as an entropy-regulation mechanism that reduces effective collapse velocity and stabilizes meaning in recursive AI systems. The work contributes a unified thermodynamic account of semantic drift, collapse velocity, and governance design for AI-mediated decision environments.

title: Cross-File Associations (CFAs): A Lightweight, Decentralized Model for Expressing File Relationships

detail.title: Cross-File Associations (CFAs): A Lightweight, Decentralized Model for Expressing File Relationships
detail.abstract: Folders, archive files, source code repositories, and similar containers are the dominant mechanisms for grouping digital artifacts today [1,2]. Containers offer clarity and durability, but they also impose rigid structure and become fragile when data moves across systems or administrative boundaries. Tagging systems provide a more flexible and decentralized alternative, but at the cost of precision and formal interpretability; prior work documents the semantic ambiguity and weak governance that arise in collaborative tagging and folksonomies [3-5]. This paper introduces Cross-File Associations (CFAs), a lightweight mechanism for declaring relationships among files and file-like objects. Like tags, CFAs allow logical groupings that do not depend on physical containment or central authority. Unlike tags, CFAs make relationships explicit and structured in ways that software can interpret reliably. CFAs are simple enough for informal use, yet expressive enough to support automation and reasoning. The paper develops the conceptual foundations of CFAs, illustrates their use through concrete examples, and situates them among existing organizational techniques.

detail.abstract: This short paper employs a two-week autoethnographic approach to investigate how the algorithmic infrastructure of Rednote (Xiaohongshu) constructs and reinforces digital identity. Focusing on the lived experience of a Chinese international student in Australia, the research documents the dynamic interplay between user interactions-such as likes, searches, and browsing pauses-and the platform's curatorial responses. The findings reveal that Rednote's algorithm functions as a form of cultural governance rather than a neutral information filter; it actively interprets user intentions, framing travel curiosity within narratives of risk and confining the user within a singular, marketable identity profile centered on specific cultural affiliations. Even when met with deliberate behavioral interventions, the system exhibits a corrective mechanism that pulls the user back into a familiar algorithmic echo chamber. The study concludes that the illusion of personalization masks a reality of algorithmic power, where the digital self is managed through emotional intimacy and disciplined by market logic.

detail.abstract: The fact that Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools are extracting data on a massive scale without compensating the authors, is undermining the current model for author remuneration. First, our research clarifies two fundamental misconceptions about the fair use of AI training data. Also, we determine the boundaries of the application of remuneration rights: it is not aimed at the AI research and development stage, but at AI models utilizing the unauthorized data, having already reached the stage of commercial application, and thereby significantly replacing the original products in the market. Our paper indicates, in line with this predicament, that the traditional copyright law encounters three structural predicaments in responding to the black box of AI: failure to give evidence, challenges in determining infringement, and inequality in the inquiry of rights protection processes. Such dilemmas result in failure in the ex post relief model. Considering this, we regard that regulation needs to change its focus to the ex ante remuneration instead of ex post responsibilities. The proposed research includes a two-track reform agenda. First, through the legal principles of food safety, we propose a mandatory disclosure of the catalog of the training data (raw material catalog) of AI companies to eliminate the problem of transparency. Second, we suggest the creation of a model of a centralized procurement with the focus on the Collective Management Organizations (CMOs) in order to attain efficient blanket licensing and value distribution. The purpose of such a system is to transform the value re-return system in the era of AI and provide the sustainability and fairness of the creative ecosystem.

title: Responsible Machine Learning Operations: Closing The Gap Between Speed And Oversight

detail.title: Responsible Machine Learning Operations: Closing The Gap Between Speed And Oversight
detail.abstract: As Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) shift from static deployment to Continuous Training (CT), organizations face an acute tension between operational velocity and model integrity. While technical pipelines are increasingly automated, governance mechanisms often lag, creating "institutional black-boxes" where decision logic is obscured by speed. To address this sociotechnical gap, this study employs a qualitative interview analysis approach to investigate how high-maturity practitioners operationalize responsibility in dynamic environments. Data was collected via asynchronous structured written interviews to capture the decision-making logic of practitioners ranging from SVPs to engineers. The findings introduce the framework of Conditional Delegation, revealing that organizations resolve the agility-safety paradox not by slowing down, but by embedding automated drift detection algorithms directly into the pipeline. This architecture enables a risk-based division of labor in which automated checks handle routine integrity conditions, while human oversight focuses on ambiguous or ethically sensitive cases. By implementing Governance-as-Code, organizations translate abstract values into executable constraints, demonstrating that high-velocity systems can maintain operational resilience. This research contributes to Information Systems literature by defining how automated mechanisms can enforce accountability without displacing necessary human discretion

title: The Economics of AI Supply Chain Regulation
affiliations: , University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management and Tsinghua University - Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management

detail.title: The Economics of AI Supply Chain Regulation
detail.abstract: The rise of foundation models has driven the emergence of AI supply chains, where upstream foundation model providers offer fine-tuning and inference services to downstream firms developing domain-specific applications. Downstream firms pay providers to use their computing infrastructure to fine-tune models with proprietary data, creating a co-creation dynamic that enhances model quality. Amid concerns that foundation model providers and downstream firms may capture excessive consumer surplus, along with increasing regulatory measures, this study employs a game-theoretic model involving a provider and two competing downstream firms to analyze how policy interventions affect consumer surplus in the AI supply chain. Our analysis shows that policies promoting price competition in downstream markets (i.e., pro-price-competitive policies) boost consumer surplus only when compute or data preprocessing costs are high, while compute subsidies are effective only when these costs are low, suggesting these policies complement each other. In contrast, policies promoting quality competition in downstream markets (i.e., pro-quality-competitive policies) always improve consumer surplus. We also find that under pro-price-competitive policies or compute subsidies, both the provider and downstream firms can achieve higher profits along with greater consumer surplus, creating a win-win-win outcome. However, pro-quality-competitive policies increase the provider's profits while reducing those of downstream firms. Finally, as compute costs decline, pro-price-competitive policies may lose their effectiveness, whereas compute subsidies may shift from ineffective to effective. These findings offer insights for policymakers seeking to foster AI supply chains that are economically efficient and socially beneficial.

title: Why More Data Does Not Produce Meaning

detail.title: Why More Data Does Not Produce Meaning
detail.abstract: A widespread assumption in discussions of artificial intelligence holds that sufficient data and computational capacity should eventually produce meaning. Under this view, the remaining barriers to understanding are scale and sophistication. This assumption is not merely overstated but structurally mistaken. The error is a category confusion: conflating the operation of generating interpretations with the constraint-bound operation of selecting one under consequence. While contemporary AI systems excel at identifying structure across large data spaces, meaning does not arise from structure alone. This paper reframes meaning as an outcome of constraint, not computation. It traces how the failure to distinguish between interpretive expansion and interpretive termination under consequence leads to persistent confusion about AI "understanding," and clarifies why more data, in itself, cannot resolve that confusion.

title: LLM Evaluations for Bharat Tax Laws ('LE-BTL'). A Framework to Evaluate and Benchmark the Accuracy of Large Language Models (‘LLMs’) in the Context of the Indian Tax Laws
affiliations: , , Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, , , ,  and

detail.title: LLM Evaluations for Bharat Tax Laws ('LE-BTL'). A Framework to Evaluate and Benchmark the Accuracy of Large Language Models (‘LLMs’) in the Context of the Indian Tax Laws
detail.abstract: LLMs are increasingly being used to support legal and tax workflows by enhancing research efficiency, facilitating compliance analysis, and automating document management. However, the intricate and evolving nature of Indian tax law, marked by frequent amendments, complex statutory interpretation, and divergent judicial precedents, requires domain-specific evaluation tools. Existing global LLM benchmarks fail to adequately assess jurisdictional legal reasoning in this context. Benchmarking serves as a critical tool for evaluating the performance and effectiveness of LLMs, ensuring that they meet the specific requirements and challenges posed by the Indian tax system. By establishing clear benchmarks, we can systematically assess the capabilities of LLMs in handling complex taxrelated queries, providing accurate interpretations, and delivering reliable outcomes. Through the paper, we present the LE-BTL framework, the first benchmark designed to systematically evaluate LLM performance in Indian tax law. Built in collaboration with tax law professionals, the benchmark uses a structured IRAC+ framework (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion, Interpretation and Justification) to evaluate models on realistic legal tasks. Twelve leading LLMs are assessed across three prompting strategies: base, persona, and fewshot persona, highlighting the interplay between model architecture, instruction tuning, and the depth of legal reasoning. Our results reveal a clear performance stratification: proprietary models such as GPT o3 Pro, GPT o3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro consistently outperform open-weight and lightweight models, especially on complex reasoning tasks. Although some recently introduced models demonstrate strong performance within agentic frameworks with tool assistance, they often fall short of delivering the level of detailed reasoning and depth of legal analysis that tax professionals expect. We also evaluated LLM-as-a-Judge by comparing GPT-4o’s scoring against human experts in tax laws and an alternative LLM judge (Gemini Flash 2.5) (code repo available at Github repository). While GPT 4o exhibits mild score inflation for top models, all three evaluators converge on relative model rankings with very high correlation, confirming the comparative reliability of LLM-based assessment frameworks. This evaluation exercise thus offers a comprehensive, explainable, and reproducible evaluation tool for legal AI in India. The evaluation prompts and scoring rubric used in LE-BTL framework closely mirror the approach a human expert would take in assessing performance. This alignment is further supported by the directional consistency observed between the model rankings produced by LLM judges GPT-4o and Gemini Flash 2.5 and those assigned by human evaluators. It provides a reliable foundation for researchers, policymakers, and legal-tech developers seeking to deploy LLMs responsibly, enhancing, rather than replacing, expert judgment in the Indian tax ecosystem.

title: CYBER-ALIGN™ Maturity Index: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework for Measurable Cyber Resilience Across Governance, Human Behavior, and Operational Controls

detail.title: CYBER-ALIGN™ Maturity Index: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework for Measurable Cyber Resilience Across Governance, Human Behavior, and Operational Controls
detail.abstract: Cybersecurity failures increasingly stem not from inadequate security tooling but from misalignment across governance, human behavior, and operational resilience. Traditional compliance-driven approaches evaluate cybersecurity effectiveness in silos, resulting in organizations that are technically "secure" yet operationally vulnerable. To address this critical gap, this study introduces the CYBER-ALIGN™ Maturity Index (CAMI) a multidimensional scoring and optimization framework designed to quantify enterprise cyber resilience as a function of alignment between policy, visibility, behavioral readiness, threat intelligence, and recovery capability. CAMI integrates five weighted dimensions GOVERN (20 percent), VISUALIZE (20 percent), EDUCATE (20 percent), PROTECT (25 percent), and RECOVER (15 percent) establishing a 0-100 maturity scale informed by diagnostic telemetry across proprietary KPIs including the Compliance Alignment Index (CAI™), Data Visibility Matrix (DVM™), Cyber Behavior Index (CBI™), Threat Readiness Gauge (TRG™), and Resilience Score (RS™). The framework is validated through cross-industry case implementations, demonstrating quantifiable improvements including reduced audit closure time, accelerated threat remediation cycles, and enhanced incident recovery performance. Results confirm that CAMI not only increases situational awareness and governance accountability but also enables predictive resilience modeling with measurable operational, financial, and regulatory outcomes. This work advances the state of cybersecurity assurance by providing an evidence-based, continuously adaptive, and executive-ready metric for cybersecurity maturity that is scalable across sectors. The CYBER-ALIGN™ Maturity Index offers a practical pathway for transforming cybersecurity posture from reactive defense to strategic resilience, supporting both compliance mandates and sustained digital trust.

detail.abstract: Growing concerns about fairness, privacy, robustness, and transparency have made it a central expectation of AI governance that automated decisions be explainable by institutions and intelligible to affected parties. We introduce the Smart Data Portfolio (SDP) framework, which treats data categories as productive but risk-bearing assets, formalizing input governance as an information-risk trade-off. Within this framework, we define two portfolio-level quantities, Informational Return and Governance-Adjusted Risk, whose interaction characterizes data mixtures and generates a Governance-Efficient Frontier. Regulators shape this frontier through risk caps, admissible categories, and weight bands that translate fairness, privacy, robustness, and provenance requirements into measurable constraints on data allocation while preserving model flexibility. A telecommunications illustration shows how different AI services require distinct portfolios within a common governance structure. The framework offers a familiar portfolio logic as an input-level explanation layer suited to the large-scale deployment of AI systems.

title: ATM Jackpotting and the Hijacking of Smart Machines: Hybrid Crimes Reveal a Cybercrime Gap

detail.title: ATM Jackpotting and the Hijacking of Smart Machines: Hybrid Crimes Reveal a Cybercrime Gap
detail.abstract: Automated Teller Machine (ATM) jackpotting is the malware-based hacking that forces ATMs to dispense cash. Jackpotting illustrates a structural gap in federal criminal law. Though increasingly common in the United States, jackpotting prosecutions rely on statutes of imperfect fir rather than legislation tailored to hybrid cyber-physical crimes. Using a "Goldilocks" framework, this Comment argues that the Computer Fraud Abuse Act (CFAA) is too narrow, the Hobbs Act too harsh, and the federal bank fraud statute nearly "just right." The CFAA reaches unauthorized access but struggles with conduct that blends digital instruction and physical cash theft. The Hobbs Act, rooted in force and fear against human victims, does not align with machine-based manipulation. By contrast, the bank fraud statute better captures schemes targeting financial institutions, though it was not drafted with cybercrime in mind. These gaps create sentencing disparities and doctrinal uncertainty where similar conduct yield inconsistent penalties. Jackpotting highlights a broader challenge: the gap in federal law when crimes blur digital and physical boundaries.

title: Product Visibility in AI-Driven Commerce: An Analysis of How Large Language Model Shopping Assistants Evaluate and Surface Ecommerce Products

detail.title: Product Visibility in AI-Driven Commerce: An Analysis of How Large Language Model Shopping Assistants Evaluate and Surface Ecommerce Products
detail.abstract: The emergence of large language model (LLM) based shopping assistants represents a fundamental shift in product discovery mechanisms within ecommerce ecosystems. Unlike traditional search engines that rely on keyword matching and link-based ranking algorithms, AI shopping assistants interpret natural language queries, evaluate product attributes through semantic understanding, and generate synthesized recommendations by querying structured product data feeds. This paper examines how AI shopping assistants form product understanding, identifies common failure modes that prevent products from appearing in AI-generated shopping answers, and analyzes the structural signals that influence AI visibility. Through analysis of current implementation patterns and product data requirements, we find that many ecommerce products fail to surface in AI shopping contexts due to incomplete attribute specification, inconsistent data standardization, inadequate schema markup, and fragmented product entity representation. The findings suggest that AI-driven product retrieval operates under fundamentally different constraints than traditional SEO optimization, requiring merchants to adopt structured data practices that enable machine interpretation rather than human readability. This research contributes to understanding the evolving technical requirements for product discoverability in AImediated commercial environments and outlines implications for ecommerce practitioners, platform operators, and future research directions.

detail.abstract: Enterprises are moving from single assistant deployments to multi-agent systems that interact across workflows, tools, and specialized software. As the number of agents grows, coordination quality becomes a primary determinant of performance, customization, and reliability. This paper models agent organizations as temporal, multi-layer socio-technical networks with explicit system boundaries and observation windows, allowing interactions among humans, agents, tools, and resource artifacts to be analyzed consistently. Using this representation, it discusses standard social network analysis (SNA) measures to enterprise agent settings to identify coordination hubs, bottlenecks, shadow dependencies, and fragile single points of failure, then interprets these signals to inform organizational design and governance choices. The paper examines the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a machine-to-software interaction layer, clarifying its current structure and contrasting MCP-mediated connectivity with human communication networks. It further positions memory as a governance lever by distinguishing short-term and long-term memory modes and proposing controlled switching between them. Finally, it introduces tier and role-based sociograms and a hybrid human-agent network perspective to support continuous optimization over time, including agent count management and persona consistency.

title: A Study on the Intersection of AI and Human Creativity

detail.title: A Study on the Intersection of AI and Human Creativity
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the landscape of creativity by augmenting artistic processes, enabling new forms of expression, and facilitating human-machine collaboration. This study conducts an exploratory analysis of AI-driven creativity across domains such as music, visual arts, writing, and design. By examining datasets, case studies, and innovation patterns, the aim is to understand how AI influences creative outcomes, democratizes artistic tools, and reshapes the role of human creators. Using data visualization, trend analysis, and literature insights, the research identifies the impact of generative models (like GPT and DALL•E), evaluates ethical concerns, and uncovers disparities in access and usage. Results show that AI tools enhance productivity, foster cocreation, and lower the barrier to entry for non-traditional artists. However, challenges remain in terms of authorship, originality, and ethical governance. The study advocates for inclusive AI development, transparency in creative processes, and hybrid models that celebrate both human and machine contributions. These findings offer a foundation for future research, policy frameworks, and educational integration of AI in the creative arts.

title: Invariant Pricing Operators in Finance III: Rough Volatility and Infinite-Dimensional Pricing Isomorphisms

detail.title: Invariant Pricing Operators in Finance III: Rough Volatility and Infinite-Dimensional Pricing Isomorphisms
detail.abstract: Rough stochastic volatility models exhibit empirical realism but violate classical Markovian and PDE-based pricing paradigms. We develop a unified invariant framework for rough volatility pricing that separates what is structural, what is obstructed, and what is computationally realizable. Our core contribution is a lifted semigroup formulation in which rough volatility pricing becomes deterministic at the level of an infinite-dimensional state. Within this framework, we establish isomorphisms between three pricing realizations: (i) a Volterra-lifted Markov semigroup, (ii) fractional Riccati and Fourier representations, and (iii) Monte Carlo estimators. These equivalences are rigorous under explicit analytic and integrability assumptions. We further show that for Hurst parameter H < 1/2, no finite-dimensional Markovian PDE realization exists, and that for H ≤ 1/4 the canonical Lyons rough-path lift required for pathwise PDE constructions is unavailable without additional structure. A formal path-integral representation is provided as an intuitionpreserving mnemonic; mathematical rigor proceeds via the lifted semigroup and Feynman-Kac constructions. The framework clarifies why disparate numerical methods agree when they do, why PDE methods fail in rough regimes, and how computational complexity depends intrinsically on regularity.

title: Invariant Pricing Operators in Finance IV: Invariant Realization Theory: Classification, Obstruction, and Complexity

detail.title: Invariant Pricing Operators in Finance IV: Invariant Realization Theory: Classification, Obstruction, and Complexity
detail.abstract: Multiple computational methods-PDE solvers, Monte Carlo simulation, Fourier inversion, lattice methods-yield identical option prices. We develop Invariant Realization Theory (IRT), a mathematical framework that organizes this phenomenon and extracts three types of content: (i) Classification: We prove that under explicit analytic and spectral admissibility conditions, including a uniform sparsity hypothesis on finite-section generators, every realization of the Black-Scholes pricing semigroup reduces to one of four normal-form equivalence classes. The classification is exhaustive within this framework. (ii) Obstruction: We establish that rough volatility models with Hurst parameter H < 1/2 admit no finite-dimensional Markovian state representation. For H ≤ 1/4, the canonical rough path lift required for pathwise PDE constructions is unavailable within the standard Lyons rough path framework. (iii) Complexity: We prove intrinsic cost-to-accuracy bounds-Θ(ε-d/2) for PDE, Θ(ε-2) for Monte Carlo, O(log(1/ε)) for Fourier with analytic payoffs-using Kolmogorov n-widths and information-based complexity. We explicitly delineate which results are new theorems, which reorganize existing mathematics, and which remain conjectural. An intertwiner discovery algorithm automatically constructs equivalence maps between discretized realizations.

title: Modern Monetary Theory, Functional Finance, and Fiscal Cycles: A Continuous-Time Macro Model with Interest-Rate Peg and Job Guarantee

detail.title: Modern Monetary Theory, Functional Finance, and Fiscal Cycles: A Continuous-Time Macro Model with Interest-Rate Peg and Job Guarantee
detail.abstract:
This paper develops a continuous-time dynamic macroeconomic model explicitly grounded in Modern Monetary Theory (MMT), taking the analytical framework established by Asada (2020) as its direct point of departure.
In this framework, the nominal interest rate is treated as an exogenous policy variable set by the central bank, money is endogenously supplied, and fiscal policy is governed by the principle of functional finance. The objective of the paper is not to reassess the basic consistency of MMT-style regimes, but to deepen their dynamic analysis and to clarify how institutional design shapes macroeconomic stability and cyclical behavior. Building on Asada (2020), the paper extends the analysis in two main directions. First, it provides a systematic characterization of endogenous cyclical dynamics within MMT-type models using Hopf bifurcation theory. While previous work has shown that coordinated fiscal and monetary policy can generate stability, instability, and cyclical fluctuations under an interest-rate peg, the present paper identifies precise threshold conditions under which a locally stable steady state loses stability and gives rise to persistent oscillations~arising from the interaction between real activity, inflation, and discretionary fiscal feedback. Second, the paper incorporates an explicit Job Guarantee (JG) program into the dynamic MMT framework. Although employment plays a central role in MMT policy discussions, it remains implicit in most formal models. The Job Guarantee is modeled as a buffer-stock mechanism for labor, introducing an automatic component of government spending that responds directly to employment shortfalls. Analytically, the presence of a Job Guarantee enlarges the region of parameter values for which the steady state is locally asymptotically stable and shifts the Hopf bifurcation boundary outward, implying that stronger discretionary fiscal reactions are required to generate endogenous cycles when an employment guarantee is in place.

title: The 2015 Fifa Scandal Revisited – Applicability as a Case Study in the World of Academia

detail.title: The 2015 Fifa Scandal Revisited – Applicability as a Case Study in the World of Academia
detail.abstract: As an academic, one of our primary responsibilities is to use the real-world to convey pertinent and digestible information to our students.  Specific to understanding the “why” behind fraud, oftentimes we look to those cases that have the highest levels of notoriety – the Theranos case would be an excellent example, as it included a narrative that seemed ripe for a Hollywood script.  But simply telling a story is not necessarily how we can best use real-world cases to reinforce the product that we are attempting to sell to our students.  Rather, it would make more sense to utilize the “lessons learned” to explore and answer questions starting with some the most basic concepts – who, what, where, when, and most importantly, why? If an academic can find the “right” cases to take advantage of within the classroom, students are more likely to have a positive, meaningful learning experience that will stay with them as they enter their professional career.

title: Understanding Liability in Tort Law: From Defenses to Animal Trespass
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.title: Understanding Liability in Tort Law: From Defenses to Animal Trespass
detail.abstract: The Law of Torts is governed by the principle that for every wrong, there is a remedy (Ubi jus ibi remedium). However, the path to obtaining a remedy is often shaped by specific legal doctrines that can either mitigate or totally absolve a defendant of liability. Two of the most significant doctrines in this regard are Contributory Negligence and Volenti non fit injuria. While both involve the conduct of the plaintiff, they operate on different legal planes—one focusing on a lapse in care and the other on a deliberate choice to accept risk.

title: Invariant Pricing Operators in Finance V: Emergent Determinism and the Constraint-Limit Principle

detail.title: Invariant Pricing Operators in Finance V: Emergent Determinism and the Constraint-Limit Principle
detail.abstract: Black-Scholes is commonly presented as the archetype of stochastic finance: prices are random, hence option prices must be probabilistic expectations. This paper develops a structurally sharper viewpoint. The defining feature of Black-Scholes is not Brownian motion; it is closure. Economic constraints (self-financing and noarbitrage) combined with a limiting law (diffusion invariance) collapse microscopic degrees of freedom, producing deterministic evolution equations for macroscopic objects (pricing operators, yield surfaces, filters, equilibrium distributions). We formalize a general "Constraint + Limit ⇒ Deterministic Functional" principle, prove it in the classical complete-market diffusion setting, and then show how the same mechanism persists-in modified form-under stochastic volatility. The Heston model becomes a canonical demonstration: determinism does not disappear; it migrates to an enlarged state space, while market incompleteness relocates nonuniqueness to the choice of volatility risk premium. We then place these results in a unifying mathematical skeleton spanning affine term structure, Kalman filtering (Riccati flows), mean-field limits, entropy projections (minimal relative entropy and Schrödinger bridges), and random matrix limits. The outcome is a single geometric message: randomness is ubiquitous at the micro level, but macroscopic finance is governed by deterministic operators once constraints and limiting regimes select the effective state.

detail.abstract: Bangladesh's rapid industrial expansion has been central to economic growth and export performance. However, conventional industrial park models based on linear production systems, fragmented governance, and inefficient resource use are increasingly misaligned with global sustainability standards and market expectations. Rising environmental pressures, compliance risks, and exposure to ESG-driven trade measures highlight the need for a more integrated approach to industrial infrastructure development. This paper examines Eco-Industrial Parks (EIPs) as a planning-led and project-delivery framework capable of transforming industrial zones into resource-efficient, competitive, and resilient production systems. Drawing on international experience from South Korea, China, and Denmark, and recent initiatives in Bangladesh such as the Green and Resilient Economic Zone (GREZ) at Mirsarai, the paper analyses policy readiness, institutional gaps, and financing constraints affecting EIP implementation. The paper argues that effective adoption of EIPs in Bangladesh depends on three interlinked factors. First, integration of EIP criteria into national planning and approval systems. Second, deployment of Public-Private Partnership models for shared green infrastructure such as central effluent treatment plants, renewable energy, and waste-to-energy facilities. Third, strengthening project governance, coordination, and performance monitoring at the industrial-zone level. By framing Eco-Industrial Parks as a project-based infrastructure delivery challenge rather than solely an environmental intervention, the paper contributes to ongoing debates on sustainable industrial development, PPP governance, and project management in emerging economies.

detail.abstract: Modern societies are increasingly organized around sound, image, and narrative systems optimized for attention and profit. While this transformation is frequently examined through technological or mediaeffects frameworks, comparatively little attention has been paid to the historical displacement of embodied spiritual infrastructures that once regulated meaning, emotion, and communal identity. This paper's original contribution lies in formally modeling spirituality as social infrastructure and demonstrating how media systems now perform equivalent regulatory functions through structurally aligned incentives rather than ideological intent. This paper argues that contemporary influence systems did not replace spirituality through deliberate design, but through functional substitution. As embodied, communal, and spiritually grounded meaning systems declined through institutionalization, suppression, and economic restructuring externally mediated systems of sound and image assumed their regulatory role. Drawing on media studies, sociology of religion, African American studies, and historical analysis, this paper conceptualizes spirituality as social infrastructure across multiple eras, examines the disruption of African American spiritual autonomy as a structurally illustrative case, and demonstrates how modern media systems now occupy the resulting vacuum. Influence and financial extraction, the paper concludes, emerge not from conspiracy or centralized intent, but from structural alignment between attention capture, profit incentives, and the erosion of internally governed meaning systems.

title: The Leverage-Inflation-Wealth Transfer Cycle

detail.title: The Leverage-Inflation-Wealth Transfer Cycle

We document the mechanisms through which policy failures translate into systemic transfers, analyze the persistence of crisis narratives, and highlight the causal chain from market interventions to labor outcomes. The contribution lies in framing macroeconomic outcomes as engineered by institutional structures, providing a defensible alternative to simplistic “market failure” explanations.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural mechanisms through which modern inflation, financial leverage, monetary policy, and asset markets systematically redistribute wealth upward. Drawing on historical crises, macroeconomic indicators, and institutional features of credit markets, it demonstrates that these outcomes are systemic and institutionally reinforced rather than the result of individual behavior, demographic factors, or isolated policy errors. The analysis further shows how media and political narratives obscure these structural drivers, fragmenting working-class solidarity and enabling persistent wealth concentration. The paper contributes a unified structural framework linking asymmetric leverage access, monetary policy transmission, and narrative fragmentation to recurring distributional outcomes across economic cycles.

title: Tanjungpinang City Government Policy in Management of Encik Puan Perak Market After Revitalization

detail.title: Tanjungpinang City Government Policy in Management of Encik Puan Perak Market After Revitalization
detail.abstract: Encik Puan Perak Market is the largest market in Tanjungpinang City. The old condition of the market caused one of the blocks to collapse and had to be revitalized. However, after the revitalization, the market was empty of sellers and buyers. There are still many empty and unoccupied stalls and los. The purpose of this study is to determine the policy of the Tanjungpinang City government in managing the Encik Puan Perak Market after revitalization in 2024, in this study using the theory of Bridgeman and Davis (2004) with the theory of public policy, namely policy as a goal, policy as a legal choice of action, and policy as a hypothesis. The method used is descriptive qualitative research with data collection techniques through observation, interviews, and documentation. The results of this study show that the Tanjungpinang City Government has created a program after seeing a market that is not operating optimally. Overall, although the Tanjungpinang City Government has implemented various programs in the management of Encik Puan Perak Market after revitalization, these efforts have not been significantly successful in restoring market crowds. Infrastructure improvements, trader organization, and hygiene policies have been implemented, but the market still faces major challenges in attracting visitors. The programs that the government has put in place are still not effective in making the market operate optimally.

title: Liquidity-Aware Portfolio Construction: A Case Study in Growth, Income, and Risk Containment

detail.title: Liquidity-Aware Portfolio Construction: A Case Study in Growth, Income, and Risk Containment
detail.abstract: This paper presents a practitioner-oriented case study of a personal investment portfolio designed to balance long-term capital appreciation, income stability, and drawdown control through intentional liquidity management. Using consolidated brokerage and banking account data as of December 2025, the study evaluates asset allocation, income contribution, and stress-test outcomes under adverse market conditions. Results show that maintaining a materially high allocation to cash and cash equivalents can significantly reduce net-worth volatility while preserving optionality for opportunistic deployment. The findings contribute to applied portfolio construction literature by framing liquidity as a first-class asset rather than residual capital.

title: Unpacking the Conditions of Reputational Herding: Implications and Evidence

detail.title: Unpacking the Conditions of Reputational Herding: Implications and Evidence
detail.abstract: We examine "reputational herding," where decision makers follow the herd to maintain or improve their reputation, rather than to make optimal decisions for the firm. We propose this as an additional mechanism for firms' mimetic behaviors. We model the mechanism and demonstrate that decision makers are less likely to herd when they have a high reputation, as it strengthens their confidence in private signals and buffers them against reputational penalties in the event of a bad outcome. Conversely, herding is more likely when experts have highly correlated information (high "signal correlation"). The model's prediction on the effect of reputation differs from previous research; the model's secondary predictions on the effect of signal correlation distinguish reputational herding from informational herding. We test the theory in the context of sell-side stock analysts and employ a difference-indifferences design to compare award-winning analysts and runners-up with similar ability to assess the impact of a reputation shock on herding behavior. The overall results are consistent with the reputational herding mechanism. We discuss several managerial implications of the model and provide recommendations regarding how to mitigate the moral hazard problem of reputational herding.

detail.abstract: This research provides an integrated, comparative analysis of the systemic collapse of education in Yemen, contextualized within the broader crises in Syria and Sudan. Utilizing a multidisciplinary framework that synthesizes data from international agencies, peer-reviewed scholarship, and ground-level assessments, the study maps the dissolution of educational access, quality, equity, and governance. The analysis reveals that while infrastructure destruction and mass displacement are universal markers, the political economy of each conflict-Yemen's fragmentation, Syria's centralized degradation, and Sudan's rapid state collapse-creates distinct paralysis patterns. A critical finding is the transformation of education from a public good into a tool of political contestation and social control, most acutely observed in curriculum politicization and the gendered exclusion of girls. The study further identifies that technology-driven solutions, while innovative, often bypass the most vulnerable, necessitating a hybrid approach. The conclusion presents a tiered recovery framework, arguing that sustainable education rebuilding is inseparable from inclusive governance and must be reconceptualized as a core component of strategic peacebuilding, not merely a humanitarian sidebar.

title: The Obsolescence of Humanity: Günther Anders' Critique of Technology, Media, And the Human Condition

detail.title: The Obsolescence of Humanity: Günther Anders' Critique of Technology, Media, And the Human Condition
detail.abstract: Günther Anders, born Günther Stern in 1902 in Breslau (now Wrocław, Poland) to a German-Jewish family, emerged as one of the 20th century's most prescient critics of technological modernity. Trained under Edmund Husserl and Martin Heidegger, Anders initially pursued phenomenology but soon diverged into a unique form of philosophical anthropology that interrogated the human condition in the shadow of industrial and atomic advancements. His seminal work, Die Antiquiertheit des Menschen (translated variably as The Obsolescence of Man or The Antiquatedness of Humanity), published in two volumes (1956 and 1980), stands as a cornerstone of this inquiry. Volume I, subtitled "On the Soul in the Age of the Second Industrial Revolution," dissects how technology renders humans obsolete, not through direct obsolescence but via a "Promethean gap" where human capacities for creation outstrip moral and imaginative faculties (Anders, 1956/1980).

title: Existential Sustainability: A Structural Approach to Anti-Extractive Tourism

detail.title: Existential Sustainability: A Structural Approach to Anti-Extractive Tourism

detail.abstract:
Current sustainable tourism scholarship largely views sustainability as a set of operational practices or certifications added to existing business models. This paper challenges that paradigm by introducing "Existential Sustainability" - a theoretical framework where community integration is not an initiative, but the structural precondition for business survival. 

Through a 19-year longitudinal single-case analysis of a US-based tour operator operating in Europe, this study examines a business model where unsustainability constitutes mechanical business failure rather than certification loss. The operator retains 72% of gross revenue within local communities - compared to industry leakage of 40-80% - while achieving 18% net margins comparable to conventional operators. By structurally constraining volume (maximum 250 guests annually in an 8,000-person town) and eliminating commission-based partnerships, the model prevents the "tourism area life cycle" decline: one destination remains stable after 19 years while a comparison destination experienced complete commercial transformation under mass tourism pressure (18 residents to 850,000 annual visitors).

This paper proposes a move beyond stakeholder management toward "structural fusion," where operator viability and community prosperity are indistinguishable.

title: Schema Epistemics: Knowledge as Constraint-Bearing Structure

detail.title: Schema Epistemics: Knowledge as Constraint-Bearing Structure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. There are no personal, financial, or organizational relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the content or conclusions of this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this work. This paper is a conceptual and theoretical analysis of governance, institutional knowledge structures, and socio-technical systems. It does not involve human subjects, patient data, interviews, surveys, experiments, or identifiable personal information.
declarations.funderStatement: The research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: In contemporary governance environments, particularly those involving complex and AI-mediated systems, formal correctness, regulatory compliance, and articulated ethical intent have proven insufficient to ensure durable, accountable outcomes. Policies, standards, and oversight mechanisms may satisfy procedural and legal requirements while nevertheless drifting, fragmenting, or collapsing under real-world conditions. This recurring failure pattern suggests a gap not merely in implementation or enforcement, but in how knowledge itself is framed within governance structures. This paper introduces Schema Epistemics, an epistemic framing in which knowledge is understood not primarily as a set of assertions, rules, or metrics, but as a constraint-bearing structure that must preserve meaning, orientation, and function under sustained use. Within this view, schemas are reusable forms that encode assumptions, boundaries, and affordances. Their epistemic legitimacy arises not solely from correctness or coherence at the point of articulation, but from structural survivability across time, context, incentives, and institutional boundaries. Schema Epistemics reframes failure as a diagnostic signal rather than an anomaly. When governance systems degrade despite formal validity, the cause is often schema degradation-the erosion or misalignment of constraints through overextension, context collapse, incentive distortion, or loss of interpretability. Crucially, such degradation can occur even when individual components remain internally consistent and compliant. The paper positions Schema Epistemics as a neutral, non-prescriptive lens applicable across governance, standards development, organizational design, and AI oversight. It does not propose new policy instruments, regulatory regimes, or alignment techniques. Instead, it offers an evaluative framework for assessing whether knowledge artifacts-such as standards, frameworks, protocols, and governance models-are capable of retaining epistemic integrity under real-world pressure. Design-Based Research (DBR) is identified as a particularly compatible observational approach within this framing, insofar as it foregrounds iterative enactment, contextual variation, and reflective refinement. However, Schema Epistemics is not itself a research methodology; it functions as an interpretive layer for understanding how structured knowledge behaves over time when embedded in institutional practice. By shifting attention from declarative validity to structural endurance, Schema Epistemics provides a foundation for governance that is resilient without being ideological, and accountable without being reductive. It enables institutions to distinguish between systems that merely satisfy formal criteria and those capable of sustaining coherent action under constraint.

detail.abstract: The growing gap between management education and industry requirements has emerged as a major concern in India’s higher education system. Although MBA programs aim to prepare students for managerial roles, employers increasingly report that graduates lack essential practical and employability skills. This study examines the skill gap between the MBA curriculum and industry expectations in India. Using a descriptive research design, the study focuses on identifying discrepancies between the skills imparted through academic coursework and the competencies demanded by organizations. The research emphasizes technical skills, soft skills, industry exposure, and employability-related competencies. Primary data will be collected through a structured questionnaire administered to MBA students and recent graduates. Simple statistical tools such as percentage analysis and mean scores will be used for data interpretation. The study aims to provide practical insights into curriculum limitations and offers recommendations for aligning management education with industry needs. The findings of this research are expected to assist academic institutions, faculty members, and policymakers in improving the relevance and effectiveness of MBA programs in India.

title: The One-Dimensional Homo Liberalius: A Marxist-Psychoanalytic Critique of Neoliberal Subjectivity in Contemporary Ukrainian Media

detail.title: The One-Dimensional Homo Liberalius: A Marxist-Psychoanalytic Critique of Neoliberal Subjectivity in Contemporary Ukrainian Media
detail.abstract:
In Herbert Marcuse's seminal work, One-Dimensional Man (1964), the Frankfurt School philosopher delineates the contours of advanced industrial society, where technological rationality subsumes human potential into a flattened, conformist existence. Under this regime, individuals are molded into "one-dimensional" beings, their critical faculties dulled by the seamless integration of production, consumption, and ideology. Marcuse argues that capitalism, far from fostering genuine freedom, perpetuates a "happy consciousness" that represses alternatives, rendering opposition impotent (Marcuse, 1964). This critique resonates profoundly in the neoliberal era, where the "techniques of the self"—as Foucault (1988) might term them—atomize subjects into entrepreneurial units, competing in a meritocratic facade that masks class exploitation.

Drawing from personal notes on contemporary Ukrainian cultural phenomena (Aleksandrovna, 2025), this essay extends Marcuse's framework through a left-oriented, Marxist-psychoanalytic lens. It posits the emergence of "Homo Liberalius"—a neoliberal counterpart to the derided "Homo Sovieticus"—as the archetypal subject of late capitalism. Unlike the Orwellian dystopia feared in the West, with its overt authoritarianism (Orwell, 1949), neoliberalism realizes a subtler totalitarianism: one of corporate culture, dumbed-down education, and commodified relationships. As Aleksandrovna (2025) observes, "was Homo Sovieticus, and this is Homo Liberalius" (p. [15.12.2025 12:30]), highlighting how Western liberalism, not Soviet engineering, has standardized humanity into system cogs.

title: Arbitrator's Limits in Commercial Contracts

detail.title: Arbitrator's Limits in Commercial Contracts
detail.abstract: The Supreme Court of India, in a landmark ruling delivered on November 7, 2025, set aside a substantial arbitral award in the matter of Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited versus M/s. Brandavan Food Products and others. The case arose from disputes concerning catering contracts for Rajdhani, Shatabdi, and Duronto Express trains, where caterers sought differential payment for serving "second regular meals" at rates prescribed for "combo meals" and claimed reimbursement for "welcome drinks" provided without separate compensation. The sole Arbitrator had awarded significant monetary relief to the caterers, which was partially upheld by the Single Judge of Delhi High Court but substantially restored by the Division Bench. However, the Supreme Court comprehensively examined whether the Arbitrator exceeded his mandate by interpreting contractual terms contrary to the binding policy directives of the Railway Board. The Court held that the arbitral award was vitiated by patent illegality under Section 34(2A) and violated public policy under Section 34(2)(b)(ii) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The judgment reaffirms that arbitral tribunals cannot rewrite contracts or interpret them contrary to explicit policy frameworks that govern the trade usages applicable to the transaction, as mandated by Section 28(3) of the Act. This decision strengthens the principle that contractual parties, especially in public sector arrangements, are bound by existing policy circulars that form the basis of their commercial agreements, and arbitrators cannot exercise hermeneutical discretion to contradict such binding frameworks.

title: Contested Governance: The Geopolitical Transformation of Semiconductor Industry Regulation in Asia

detail.abstract:
Through an analysis of semiconductor industry regulations in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, China, and Singapore, this paper demonstrates how
traditional market-oriented regulatory approaches have been supplanted by complex geopolitical issues with significant consequences. It reveals that
semiconductor regulation in these countries increasingly operates at the intersection of multiple policy domains—industrial development, national
security, environmental protection, and international relations—necessitating sophisticated coordination mechanisms to address inherent conflicts and tradeoffs.
Drawing on theoretical frameworks including polycentric governance, reflexive law, global production network analysis, and strategic trade theory, it
provides an interdisciplinary perspective on this evolving regulatory landscape, highlighting four key challenges: balancing security with innovation, mitigating supply chain risks, addressing fragmentation versus harmonization of standards, and tackling sustainability concerns. It concludes by proposing regulatory approaches that can maintain the advantages of global semiconductor integration while addressing legitimate security issues, supply chain vulnerabilities, and environmental challenges.

detail.abstract: A rapid transition to low-carbon production is essential for climate mitigation, but its economic costs and benefits are not evenly shared. This paper studies how carbon pricing affects workers of different skills when clean and dirty energy sectors differ in their skill intensity. We extend a dynamic multi-sector environmental growth model in the spirit of Golosov et al. (2014) by introducing high-and low-skill households and a production structure in which clean energy is relatively high-skill intensive and dirty energy relatively low-skill intensive. We show that a Pigouvian carbon tax decentralizes the first-best allocation by internalizing the external cost of emissions, yet it is not distributionally neutral: the induced reallocation of capital and labour toward clean production raises the skill premium and can reduce welfare for the low-skill household. Numerical simulations calibrated to the U.S. economy confirm that aggregate welfare gains coexist with significant welfare losses for low-skill households, raising concerns about the political acceptability of such policies.

detail.abstract: Since the implementation of the Companies Act (2013), India has witnessed a massive infusion of corporate capital into the social sector, estimated at over ₹25,000 crore annually. However, empirical evidence suggests this spending is plagued by allocative inefficiency: funds are disproportionately concentrated in industrialized states and "safe" sectors like education, while critical needs in aspirational districts remain unmet. This paper argues that this imbalance is not merely a result of strategic intent but a failure of market designspecifically, high search frictions and information asymmetry between corporate donors and implementation agencies. Departing from traditional signaling models, this study conceptualizes the CSR ecosystem as a two-sided matching market. We propose a theoretical framework based on the Gale-Shapley Deferred Acceptance Algorithm to model how firms (seeking brand-cause congruence) and social projects (seeking stable capital) can be matched efficiently. We demonstrate that a centralized clearinghouse-a "National CSR Exchange"-can resolve coordination failures, minimize herding behavior, and maximize aggregate social welfare. The findings offer actionable policy insights for moving Indian CSR from mere compliance to strategic, welfare-maximizing impact.

title: Public Mining and Gas for National Wealth and Fiscal Sovereignty: A Proposal for Transparent, Market-Based, and Sovereign Resource Management

The model is explicitly pro-competition, encouraging private firms to participate in extraction, refining, and distribution, while maintaining public ownership of the underlying assets. title: TZHE — Training Zone Hypermodel Evaluation: An ITSA-Based Hypermodel Framework for Training ROI Assessment with Skill Decay

detail.title: TZHE — Training Zone Hypermodel Evaluation: An ITSA-Based Hypermodel Framework for Training ROI Assessment with Skill Decay
detail.abstract: Evaluating the effectiveness and return on investment (ROI) of corporate training programs remains a persistent challenge due to the absence of explicit counterfactuals, the temporal degradation of skills, and the fragmentation of evaluation practices across learning formats. Traditional before-after comparisons and survey-based approaches systematically underestimate training effects by ignoring both baseline trajectories and post-training skill decay. This paper introduces TZHE (Training Zone Hypermodel Evaluation), a structured, quasi-experimental evaluation framework for training ROI assessment. TZHE is built on Interrupted Time Series Analysis (ITSA) augmented with parametric exponential skill decay and organized as a zone-based hypermodel. The framework treats training outcomes as investments in depreciating human capital assets and decomposes the total training effect into two canonical components: immediate performance gains and avoided losses due to skill decay. TZHE is explicitly defined as an evaluation protocol rather than a novel statistical estimator. ITSA serves as the causal identification core, while the hypermodel layer standardizes parameter extraction, normalization, monetary aggregation, and scenario-based interpretation across heterogeneous training schemes. Differences between training formats-such as onboarding, compliance programs, hard skills, soft skills, leadership, or certification programs-are encoded through parameterization and hyperparameters rather than through distinct model structures, ensuring comparability and scalability. The proposed framework is statistically testable, explainable to non-technical stakeholders, and directly implementable in analytical pipelines and decision-support calculators. TZHE is applicable to individual-, group-, and organization-level metrics and provides a reproducible foundation for both ex-post evaluation and ex-ante ROI forecasting of training interventions.

detail.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive assessment of India's potential output and output gap using three widely applied methods: the Hodrick-Prescott (H.P) filter, the Christiano-Fitzgerald (C.F) filter, and a production function (PF) approach. These methods are applied on KLEMS data from Reserve Bank of India, for the period 1980 to 2022. All three methods identify the major turning points associated with the 1991 crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 shock, though they differ in the magnitude and persistence of cyclical fluctuations. A detailed timedomain analysis shows that the HP cycle is the smoothest with mild mean reversion, the PF cycle exhibits moderate persistence and economically intuitive adjustments, and the CF cycle displays sharp oscillations and strong negative autocorrelations. Descriptive statistics reveal that the PF cycle is moderately volatile with relatively balanced tail behaviour, while the HP and CF cycles show greater skewness and kurtosis. Correlation analysis indicates high coherence among the three approaches, particularly between the HP and PF cycles. Unit root tests confirm that all cyclical components are stationary, validating their interpretation as shortrun deviations from trend. Overall, the results highlight that output gap estimates are sensitive to the choice of methodology, with each approach emphasizing different aspects of the underlying cyclical behaviour. The results highlight the importance of a multi-method approach for assessing India's potential output and output gap, especially during times of macroeconomic crisis and structural transformation.

title: HALF-STAR: Feedback Loops of Collapse and Resilience – A Framework for Diagnosing Spirals of Instability and Designing Resilient Systems

detail.title: HALF-STAR: Feedback Loops of Collapse and Resilience – A Framework for Diagnosing Spirals of Instability and Designing Resilient Systems
detail.abstract: Systems succeed or fail not only because of strategy, leadership, or luck, but because of the feedback loops that drive their behaviour. Some loops amplify themselves: small actions snowball into momentum, dependence, and eventually breakdown. Others counteract strain: buffers, pacing, and correction turn pressure into stability. This paper introduces the HALF-STAR framework – two opposing feedback cycles. HALF (Hook, Amplification, Lock-in, Fracture) describes how systems spiral into runaway momentum and eventual breakdown. STAR (Strain, Tempering, Adjustment, Resolve) describes how systems absorb pressure and turn it into resilience. Together, they offer a simple grammar for seeing whether a system is spiralling out of control or stabilising itself. Drawing on behavioural economics and examples from finance, technology, and organisations, the paper shows how HALF loops fuel bubbles, addictive platforms, AI over-reliance, and organisational overreach, while STAR loops stabilise systems through pacing, openness, redundancy, and deliberate friction. The core insight is straightforward: fragility is designed through reinforcing loops left unchecked; resilience is built by installing brakes before momentum becomes a trap. By learning to spot whether a system amplifies or corrects pressure, leaders can anticipate where fracture is likely-and build structures that endure.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the rapidly growing participation of young retail traders in Futures and Options (F&O) derivatives markets through the lens of behavioural finance and gambling psychology. The purpose is to demonstrate that, for many inexperienced participants, the process of F&O trading closely mirrors the psychological mechanisms established in casino gambling, rather than disciplined investment. Key behavioural finance concepts explored include overconfidence, loss aversion, and the illusion of control. We identify parallels such as variable reward schedules, intermittent reinforcement, and the subsequent dopamine-driven excitement that leads to loss chasing. Analysis of market data and trading behaviour suggests that the structural and technological environment of modern F&O trading, characterized by high leverage and rapid feedback, is highly conducive to these psychological biases. The paper highlights the specific vulnerability of young retail traders, who often lack experience and are influenced by social media narratives promoting quick wealth. The core observation is that the instrument itself is neutral, but its high-risk, high-frequency nature, when combined with human psychological vulnerabilities, transforms the trading process into a form of high-stakes speculation driven by emotion. The implications underscore an urgent need for targeted behavioural education to promote disciplined risk management and long term financial wellbeing among this demographic.

detail.abstract:
With the maturation of generative artificial intelligence models, human civilization faces not an information crisis, but a synchronization crisis. This monograph proposes a unified theory of Cognitive Divergence: the phenomenon whereby the speed of machine processing outpaces the biological and institutional adaptive capacity of humans and societies, leading to severe social and geopolitical stratification.
Synthesizing four years of theoretical research and data analysis (including reports from GitKraken, DORA, McKinsey), the work demonstrates that AI adoption is not uniform but generates three distinct cognitive classes:
L1 (The Passengers): Dependent users characterized by cognitive atrophy and the "uncertainty-reassurance cycle."
L2 (The Operators): Functionaries maintaining existing systems but exposed to maximum automation risk.
L3 (The Architects): A narrow elite entering cognitive symbiosis (Homo Symbioticus), achieving exponential productivity gains.
At a macro level, the book analyzes the "Collision of Chronologies" between major powers (US Velocity vs. EU Regulation vs. China Control) and introduces the concept of Cognitive Colonization - the process by which infrastructure-poor states become processing peripheries subject to instant "Brain Extraction." From a physical perspective, it formulates the {1=1} Equation, predicting the Q2 2027 moment when local hardware parity with cloud capabilities offers a critical window for sovereignty.
Finally, the work proposes an architectural solution: Minimal Ethical Governance (MEG). This is a technical protocol (a "TCP/IP of Cognition") based on three pillars: Radical Transparency (Audit Log), Active Cognitive Protection (MSC Mechanism), and Verifiability (DAI/ISR). Relying on Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) theory, the study argues that global system stability depends on maintaining a critical mass of over 66% rational actors (L3) as the only evolutionarily stable strategy against systemic collapse.

detail.abstract: Electronic dissemination of corporate filings via the SEC’s EDGAR system is a cornerstone of modern capital markets. Nevertheless, the SEC has also continued to accept certain filings on paper and not post them to EDGAR. Instead, they make these “hidden” disclosures available to the public in the SEC Reading Room where a private data vendor digitizes the filings and sells them to institutional clients. In April 2020, the SEC closed the Reading Room in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and began publicly disclosing scanned images of some paper filings. I examine the consequences of this SEC policy change using an archived dataset of digitized paper filings from 2018 to 2021. After the policy change, I find a pronounced equity market reaction to the content of the paper filings, a decline in information asymmetry at affected firms, and an economically and statistically significant decline in opportunism by insiders. Based on the processing costs framework from prior literature, my findings suggest that awareness costs can be a significant friction that precludes investors from accessing disclosures useful for valuation and monitoring—even when the benefits of doing so far exceed the acquisition and integration costs.

title: Leading Without the Title: How Early Career Professionals Shape Organizational Culture

detail.title: Leading Without the Title: How Early Career Professionals Shape Organizational Culture
detail.abstract: Leadership is often associated with formal authority, titles, and hierarchical power. Yet across modern organizations, meaningful influence is frequently exercised by individuals who do not hold leadership positions. This paper examines how emerging professionals contribute to organizational culture, performance, and alignment through influence rather than authority. Drawing from applied leadership theory, organizational behavior concepts, and real world observations within a complex, high reliability public sector environment, this research analyzes how communication, accountability, judgment, and initiative shape leadership outcomes from non managerial roles. The findings demonstrate that leadership without a title is not incidental but essential to organizational effectiveness. A practical, behavior based framework is introduced to illustrate how emerging professionals build credibility, influence decision making, and support leadership objectives without formal power. The paper concludes with implications for organizations seeking to develop leadership capacity earlier in the career lifecycle and for professionals navigating influence within structured environments.

title: Anti-Capitalism in American Comedic Sitcoms Post 9/11: Malcolm in the Middle, How I Met Your Mother, And Brooklyn 99

detail.title: Anti-Capitalism in American Comedic Sitcoms Post 9/11: Malcolm in the Middle, How I Met Your Mother, And Brooklyn 99
detail.abstract: This research paper examines the prevalence of anti-capitalist themes in three popular American sitcoms: Malcolm in the Middle, How I Met Your Mother, and Brooklyn 99. The purpose of this academic paper is to analyse how media (especially television) integrate conspicuous or subtle critiques of capitalism through character development, plot devices, and dialogue. The question guiding this study is to what extent American comedic sitcoms post 9/11 such as Malcolm in the Middle, How I Met Your Mother, and Brooklyn 99 reflect growing anti-capitalist ideologies in the United States of America. Sitcoms hold significance beyond entertainment, serving as social commentary that mirrors and comments on current issues or realities of the period in which they were created. By examining these TV shows, the data provides insight on how corporate greed, unethicalness motivated by the system, racial inequality, working class struggles and the illusion of the American Dream are portrayed in mainstream media. A content analysis was used for coding episodes from the beginning, middle, and end of each show, identifying whether anti-capitalist themes mentioned previously were seen. Episodes were coded (+) for these themes and (-) if not, ultimating flagging 77 episodes out of 355 studied. Findings suggest that Malcolm in the Middle critiques class disparities and the American Dream the most, How I Met Your Mother highlights environmental exploitation in capitalism and corporate greed, and Brooklyn 99 focuses on systemic racial bias and immoral behaviors. The data found illustrates that anti-capitalist themes are immersed in modern sitcoms. This research paper provides a strong foundation for further studies into media entertainment's role in social and political commentary, and the place it has as a cultural text.

detail.abstract: Professional advancement is a critical mechanism for cultivating employee development, yet limited research has examined its effects in rural banking institutions in the Philippines. A noticeable gap exists in understanding how professional development initiatives such as training programs, workshops, and mentorship impact employee outcomes in smaller, community-based banks. This study aimed to investigate the correlation between professional advancement opportunities and employee development, focusing on job satisfaction, productivity, and motivation among rural bank employees in Northern Mindanao. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed, using survey questionnaires to collect data from 32 employees. The data were analyzed to determine the relationship between professional advancement initiatives and employee development outcomes. Key findings revealed that training, workshops, and mentorship significantly enhanced job satisfaction, productivity, and motivation. The results highlight the importance of tailored professional development strategies in rural banks to foster a skilled, motivated, and engaged workforce, providing practical guidance for employee growth programs.

detail.abstract: Australian income investors face a persistent allocation challenge: cash rates are volatile, traditional fixed income embeds significant duration risk, and securitised credit-despite its systemic importance-lacks transparent, portfolio-level benchmarking frameworks. Existing indices predominantly measure issuance volume or tranche-level performance, offering limited insight into how securitised exposure is combined and maintained in a practical portfolio. This paper introduces the Australian Securitised Capital Output Tracker (ASCOT), a structural framework for representing securitised income exposure through a capital-stack lens. ASCOT separates exposure into senior and mezzanine layers, defining three fixed-weight variants (Core, Balance, and Plus) to reflect distinct structural roles rather than performance optimisation. By establishing a deterministic, rules-based allocation framework anchored in public market proxies, the framework provides a replicable benchmark for the asset class without relying on manager discretion or opaque private valuations.

detail.abstract: CRV Cosmogenesis is a mythopoetic text composed of ten movements that narrate the genesis of world, relation, and value. While the text appears at first glance to be a cosmological narrative, its deeper function is structural: it encodes a generative logic through which Conduct, Relation, and Virtue (CRV) emerge as the fundamental operators of meaning and organization. This article develops a structural theory based on the CRV cosmogenesis, treating the ten movements not as metaphysical claims but as epistemic data that reveal an underlying mechanism of ontological formation. Using a structural–hermeneutic method, the study analyzes how primordial indeterminacy crystallizes into differentiated fields of action, relational density, and evaluative orientation. The findings suggest that CRV constitutes a triadic generative engine through which phenomena acquire coherence and normativity. This triadic structure is shown to be applicable not only to cosmological interpretation but also to organizational theory, ethics, and knowledge formation. By positioning a mythopoetic text as a site of epistemic insight, this paper proposes a new mode of theorizing—generative structural philosophy—that integrates narrative, structure, and conceptual rigor. The result is a foundational contribution to emerging discussions in process ontology, relational theory, and value formation. The CRV framework offers scholars a novel pathway for analyzing how worlds—cosmic, social, organizational, and experiential—come into being through the simultaneous emergence of conduct, relation, and virtue.

detail.abstract:
Government-contracted construction projects play a critical role in India’s infrastructure development; however, contractors operating in this sector frequently experience financial stress despite executing technically viable and contractually profitable projects. This paper examines how institutional payment delays, security deposit requirements, and procedural inefficiencies embedded within government procurement systems generate persistent working-capital constraints that undermine contractor liquidity and project sustainability.

Using a qualitative–analytical approach supported by project-level financial illustrations, documented case evidence from central and municipal government projects, arbitration and court records, and comparative process analysis, the study estimates how extended payment cycles convert nominal project margins into negative cash flows. The analysis demonstrates that smaller and mid-sized contractors are disproportionately affected, often facing peak working-capital exposure of 70–80 percent of project value under delayed payment conditions, resulting in heavy reliance on high-cost bridge financing.

The paper further evaluates institutionally feasible reforms, including parallel approval workflows, milestone-based digital verification, rationalization of security deposit mechanisms, and enforceable payment timelines. Scenario-based comparisons indicate that such reforms can significantly reduce payment cycles, lower financing costs, and restore project-level financial viability without increasing fiscal burden on government agencies.

By linking administrative process design to contractor financial outcomes, this study contributes to the literature on construction finance and public procurement and offers actionable insights for policymakers, contracting authorities, financial institutions, and infrastructure developers seeking to improve execution efficiency and contractor sustainability in government-led construction programs.

title: The Assessment of Quality Control and Management Practices in Carinderias Around Barangay Calumpang, General Santos City
